name: Service Definition
purpose: Represent a durable provider-accountable commitment to produce a defined outcome for a consumer scope, with effective-dated realization bindings and typed service dependencies, while delegating offering, entitlement, request, fulfilment, service-level and observation lifecycles.

owns: durable service identity and immutable definition versions
expected outcome semantics and consumer scope
delegates: commercial or internal offering terms to the shared Offering Catalogue candidate
subscription and recurring consumption to WM-ECO-022
requests and service cases to WM-ACT-021 or the applicable request authority
delivery and fulfilment episodes to external activity or transaction masters
service-level objectives and reliability evaluation to WM-SFT-016
measured values and observations to WM-MAT-008
excludes: price eligibility channel hours or capacity terms
request case or delivery episode state
live runtime endpoint status instance counts or copied metrics
API endpoint or software component identity
a second product offering or entitlement aggregate

relations.purpose: Resolve accountable provider and realization-provider organization identity.
Resolve a delivery workflow without copying process definition or execution state.
Resolve recurring subscription or consumption relationships.
Resolve service requests or cases without importing their lifecycle.
Resolve service-level objectives and reliability evaluation.
Resolve measured quality observations without copying values into the service definition.

operations.effect: Issue a successor while preserving prior references.
Create an effective-dated provider and realization binding.
End a binding without deleting history.
Assert a typed scoped service-to-service dependency.
Retire new use while preserving historical obligations and references.

invariants: Service identity is based on expected outcome, consumer scope and provider accountability rather than one endpoint or implementation.
Consumer and technical API client are distinct roles.
Outcome semantics are declared once on the service definition and realizations do not restate them.
A service contains no runtime endpoint status, instance count or copied live metric.
Expected outcome, committed level and observed result remain separate facts.
Offering terms own price, eligibility, channels, hours and capacity; an internal offering may be explicitly unpriced.
One service may have multiple effective providers and realizations only through qualified bindings.
Every realization binding pins one immutable service-definition version and has scope, validity and authority.
Replacing an endpoint or implementation does not change service identity when outcome, consumer scope and accountability remain stable.
Service dependencies are directional, typed, version-pinned and validity-scoped.
Infrastructure or component dependencies never become service dependencies implicitly.
Request, entitlement, fulfilment, SLA and observation events never mutate service identity automatically.
Retired services and superseded realization bindings remain resolvable for historical queries.
Access to service references cannot exceed access to the linked consumer, provider or evidence records.
